heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

CENTRAL LOMBOK REGENCY

WEST NUSA TENGGARA PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL LOMBOK REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Central Lombok Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Central Lombok.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the region.
5. Implementation of Protection is all actions and service efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of children and women organized by the Regional Government and the Community.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
7. Violence against women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is that which results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, Courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from violence and discrimination.

heading: Article 2
Article 3
Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. Women's Empowerment,
b. Protection of Women;
c. Fulfillment of Children's rights; and
d. Special Protection of Children.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 5

Implementation of Women's Empowerment, includes:
a. efforts to raise awareness and shape women's behavior in the need for self-capacity enhancement;
b. efforts to develop women's access to participate in economic, political, social, and cultural fields, and
c. efforts to improve women's competence.

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

1. Efforts to raise awareness and shape women's behavior in the need for self-capacity enhancement as referred to in Article 5 letter a, include:
a. understanding and awareness of women's basic rights,
b. providing motivation to women to have ability or empowerment, and
c. fostering awareness in women about equality and their position.
2. Efforts to raise awareness and shape women's behavior as referred to in paragraph (1), are implemented through guidance of community groups, women's forums, women's organizations, and women's institutions.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out in the form of education, socialization, and advocacy.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Efforts to increase women's competence as referred to in Article 5 letter c, are carried out through, among others:
a. skills training, and
b. education and literacy for women.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 9

The implementation of Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. efforts to improve family quality,
b. efforts to fulfill the special needs of women,
c. efforts to prevent and Protect Women victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination quickly, in an integrated and integrated manner, and
d. efforts to Protect Women in disaster situations.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Efforts to improve family quality as referred to in Article 9 letter a, are implemented through:
a. improving the quality of children through providing access to information, education, counseling, and services regarding child care, nurturing, Protection, and development,
b. improving the quality of adolescents through providing access to information, education, counseling, and services regarding family life,
c. improving the functioning, role, and duties of the family,
d. empowering vulnerable families through Protection and assistance and/or facilitation to develop themselves to be equal with other families,
e. improving the quality of the family environment,
f. increasing access and opportunities to receive information and family economic resources: and
g. developing innovative ways through assistance and/or facilitation that are more effective for pre-prosperous families, and developing programs and activities in efforts to reduce poverty rates for pre-prosperous families and women who serve as heads of families.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Efforts to fulfill the special needs of women as referred to in Article 9 letter b, are implemented through:
a. health services, especially family planning services, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum,
b. fulfillment of the right to obtain paid leave including maternity leave, and
c. provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women.

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Efforts to prevent and Protect Women victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination as referred to in Article 9 letter c, include:
a. prevention of women from becoming victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination;
b. handling of women victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination; and
c. Empowerment of Women victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

Efforts to Protect Women in disaster situations as referred to in Article 9 letter d, are implemented through:
a. health services, and
b. provision of women-friendly facilities at disaster evacuation sites.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

FULFILLMENT OF CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 14

Fulfillment of Children's Rights as referred to in Article 4 letter c, includes:
a. fulfillment of civil rights and freedoms;
b. fostering family environment and alternative care;
c. fulfillment of basic health rights and welfare, and
d. fulfillment of education rights, leisure time, culture, and recreation.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Fulfillment of civil rights and freedoms as referred to in Article 14 letter a, is implemented through:
a. facilitation of population administration and civil registration of children,
b. provision of Child-appropriate information, and
c. increasing children's participation in development.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

Facilitation of population administration and civil registration of Children as referred to in Article 15 letter a, among others:
a. facilitation of ownership of birth certificate extracts;
b. facilitation of ownership of family cards, and
c. facilitation of child identity cards.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. Provision of Child-appropriate information as referred to (1) in Article 15 letter b, includes efforts to:
a. provide broad access to information for Children;
b. provide appropriate information for Children;
c. encourage the production and dissemination of Children's books; and
d. develop Protection of Children from inappropriate information.
2. In order to provide broad access to information for Children as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, analog information facilities and digital information facilities are built and developed.

heading: Article 18
Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Fostering family environment and alternative care (1) as referred to in Article 14 letter b, is implemented through:
a. fostering families or substitute families;
b. holistic and integrative early childhood development; and
c. fostering prevention of Child marriage.
2. Fostering families or substitute families as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, includes:
a. fostering the fulfillment of Children's Rights needed during their care, and
b. fostering to always include love and affection in child care.
3. Forms of fostering families or substitute families as referred to in paragraph (2), among others:
a. provision of family consultation institutions for Child care;
b. fostering standardization of alternative care institutions; and
c. strengthening the capacity of consultation institutions providing Child care services.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. Fulfillment of basic health and welfare as referred to in Article 14 letter c, includes:
a. provision of facilities and infrastructure for Child health;
b. provision of human resources in the health sector;
c. guidance on Protection and maintenance of Child health, covering:
1\. guidance on child growth health in efforts to reduce infant mortality rates and malnutrition rates for children,
2\. guidance on early breastfeeding initiation, exclusive breast milk and continuous breast milk directly,
3\. guidance on complete immunization for children, and
4\. guidance on healthy, balanced, and safe food for Children.
d. provision of facilities and infrastructure for Child welfare, covering:
1\. guidance on child-friendly households,
2\. provision of child-friendly public spaces,
3\. guidance on availability of child-friendly infrastructure in public spaces,
4\.guidance on organizing Children's playgrounds,
5\.guidance on Child care facilities,
6\.guidance on availability of breastfeeding (lactation) rooms;
7\. guidance on availability of child-friendly places of worship,
8\. provision and guidance on availability of green open spaces,
9\. guidance on organizing smoke-free areas, and
10\. guidance on organizing child-friendly public transportation,
e. provision of facilities and infrastructure for accessibility for Children with disabilities,
f. maintenance, care, and social rehabilitation of neglected children,
g. guidance on improving the welfare of poor families.
2. Guidance on child-friendly households as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d number 1, is carried out in efforts to fulfill access to clean water and proper sanitation.

heading: Article 21
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

SPECIAL PROTECTION FOR CHILDREN

Part One

General

heading: Article 22
Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

The implementation of Special Protection for Children as referred to in Article 22 paragraph (1), includes:
a. Prevention, and
b. Handling.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Prevention

heading: Article 24
Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. Optimization of child resource capacity as referred to in Article 4 letter a is carried out through:
a. increasing awareness and attitudes of children regarding the right to receive Protection;
b. increasing child participation in child Protection efforts; and
c. increasing spaces and communities that support children to grow and develop optimally, both in formal and informal environments in line with the development of information, technology, and children's situations.
2. Increasing awareness and attitudes of children regarding the right to receive Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out through regional government policy intervention toward optimization of child Protection implementation in school education.
3. Increasing child participation in child Protection efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is carried out through regional policy intervention:
a. providing and strengthening peer counselors and Youth Posyandu starting from the village/sub-district level to the district level integrated with the formal referral system,
b. providing formal participation mechanisms for children and adolescents to be directly involved in child Protection efforts at various levels, one of which is through the Children's Forum, and
c. strengthening the Children's Forum as pioneers and reporters.

heading: Article 26
Article 27
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Strengthening of regulations and institutions as referred to (1) in Article 24 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. strengthening the institutional capacity of child Protection and empowerment and education units,
b. encouraging the establishment of village regulations and village head regulations on child Protection,
c. conducting evaluations of village regulations, school regulations and/or awiq-awiq that encourage violence and vulnerability in children, and
2. Strengthening the institutional capacity of child Protection and empowerment and education units as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out through local government policy intervention towards improving the knowledge and skills of law enforcement officers, village apparatus, KUA officers, customary leaders, extension workers and teachers.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Strengthening stakeholder coordination as referred to in Article 24 letter e shall be carried out through strategies focused on:
a. improving cross-sectoral, cross-field, and cross-regional cooperation;
b. strengthening data and information systems, and
c. supervision, monitoring, and evaluation.
2. Strengthening stakeholder coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through local government policy intervention towards:
a. strengthening coordination forums for planning and implementing child Protection policies,
b. utilization of data for policy improvement, and
c. building data and information systems as a basis for implementing referral services for children requiring special Protection.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Handling

heading: Article 30
Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

In order to carry out handling in the effort of Special Protection for Children, the Regional Government needs to provide a children's social protection house/comprehensive integrated child safe house.

heading: CHAPTER VI
CHAPTER VII
Article 34
CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

PARTICIPATION OF THE COMMUNITY AND BUSINESS SECTOR

Part One

Community Participation

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

Community participation in the empowerment and Protection of Women may be carried out through:
a. provision of skills training;
b. prevention of women from becoming victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination, and
c. assistance to women victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination.

heading: Article 36
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Business Sector Participation

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

Business sector participation in the empowerment and Protection of Women may be carried out through:
a. provision of facilities and infrastructure for the empowerment and Protection of Women;
b. facilitation of education and training, and
c. provision of awards.

heading: Article 38
CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

AWARDS

Article 39

1. The Regent may grant awards to Regional Apparatus, Village/Sub-district Governments, the business sector, and the community who have actively played a role in:
a. support and active participation in efforts for women's empowerment, and
b. provision of facilitation for the protection of women and children.
2. The granting of awards as referred to in paragraph (2) (1) shall be in the form of:
a. Incentives, grants or financial assistance;
b. certificates,
C. trophies, and/or
d. facilitation of the development of facilities and infrastructure for the protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 40

Financing for the implementation of Child Protection shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 41

1. UPTD PPA that has been established before this regional regulation is promulgated shall continue to carry out its duties and functions related to the Protection of women and children and must adjust to this regional regulation no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional regulation.
2. In the event that UPTD PPA has not been established, the establishment of UPTD PPA shall be carried out no later than 2 (two) years from the promulgation of this regional regulation.
3. In the event that UPTD PPA has not been established as referred to in paragraph (2), the implementation of Integrated Services in the region shall be carried out by the regional work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 42

Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency Number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of Children and Women Victims of Violence, shall be revoked and declared invalid.

heading: Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Central Lombok Regency.

heading: GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL LOMBOK REGENCY
translated_text:
GENERAL
l. Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of children and women victims of violence has been in force for approximately 14 years. During the period of its validity, there have been many changes in policies and legislation in the field of Protection of children and women, whether adopted by the central government, provincial government or Central Lombok regency government. Therefore, at the regency regional regulation level, adjustments need to be made so that the Central Lombok regency government has a legal basis in implementing policies and programs in the field of Protection of women and children.

The field of regional government has undergone changes with the revocation of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government by Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. Based on article 12 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection constitute Mandatory Government Affairs that are not related to Basic Services. In the appendix to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the division of regency government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is regulated in more detail. The field of women includes the following authorities: a). Prevention of violence against women involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b). Provision of services for women victims of violence requiring coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing Protection services for women at the regency/city Region level. The Field of Women's Quality of Life includes, Institutionalization of Gender Mainstreaming at government institutions at the regency/city Region level. b. Empowerment of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency/city Region level. The Field of Fulfillment of Children's Rights (PHA), includes: Institutionalization of PHA in government, non-government, and business institutions at the regency/city Region level, Strengthening and development of institutions providing services to improve the quality of life of children at the regency/city Region level. The field of special child Protection includes,
a. Prevention of violence against children involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b. Provision of services for children requiring special Protection that require coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening the development of institutions providing services for children requiring special Protection at the regency/city Region level.

Changes have also occurred in law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children through two amendments, namely 1). law number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to law number concerning Protection of children, and 2. Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 Concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 Concerning Protection of Children into Law. There are a number of obligations of regional governments contained in this law that must be further regulated by regional regulations. Amendments to law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children certainly have legal implications for child Protection legal policies in Central Lombok regency.

In the aspect of Protection of women, significant changes occurred when law number 12 of 2022 concerning criminal acts of sexual violence was enacted. There are several provisions related to the obligations of regional governments that must be regulated in regional regulations: 1). Provisions of Article 76 paragraph (2) Provincial and regency/city Regional Governments are obliged to establish UPTD PPA which organizes Handling, Protection, and Recovery of Victims, Families of Victims, and/or Witnesses, 2). Article 79 paragraph (1) the obligation of the Central Government and Regional Governments to organize Prevention of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence quickly, in an integrated and integrated manner. 3). Article 80 paragraph (1) Regional Governments are obliged to organize education and training for law enforcement officials, government service personnel, and service personnel at Community-Based Service Provider Institutions, 4). Article 82 The Central Government and Regional Governments are obliged to conduct regular and continuous coordination for Victims.

At the provincial government level, Regional Regulation of West Nusa Tenggara Province Number 8 of 2015 concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children has been enacted. There are several obligations contained in the Regional Regulation related to regency obligations. 1). formation of regional regulations and regional head regulations in regencies/cities concerning Protection of Women and Children, 2). Formation of a Coordination Team for Protection of Women and Children at the regency/city level.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL LOMBOK REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "the principle of respect for human dignity" is recognition of the dignity of Victims that must be protected, respected, and upheld.

Letter b
What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is respecting equality of status without distinguishing, both parties, on the basis of religion, race, ethnicity, nationality, skin color, social status, affiliation, and ideology.

Letter c
What is meant by "the principle of the best interests of the Victim" is that all actions concerning Victims carried out by executive institutions, legislative institutions, judicial institutions, and the Community must be the primary consideration.

Letter d
What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that the subject matter related to Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence must reflect fair and proportional treatment for every citizen.

Letter e
What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that the subject matter related to Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence is able to provide broad benefits for the interests of the Community, nation, and state.

Letter f
What is meant by "the principle of legal certainty" is that the implementation of regulation of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence must be carried out within the framework of a rule of law that prioritizes the foundation of laws and regulations, propriety, and justice.
